source.citation: "The First Presbyterian Church. Indiana Avenue and Twenty-First Street (1887)." Halftone plate facing p. 82 in Philo Adams Otis, The First Presbyterian Church, 1833-1913: A History of the Oldest Organization in Chicago (Chicago: Fleming H. Revell, 1913).
what_it_does_not_supply: the north and east sides and the plan behind the front: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 35 supplies the plan
dimensions: no scale is printed; lengths come from the 1911 sheet's trace
the 21st Street flank, which the book's 1912 plate (scan leaf n116, facing p. 76) shows from the south-east and which is not yet read
what_it_supplies: the west front's gable, its width against the 1911 sheet's trace and its apex's height
the tower's place at the south-west corner, its three stages' heights, the height of its masonry and the spire's height
the composition of the west front and the tower's openings, for other work
